source.text: ÜDVÖZÖLLEK SZAKADT PATENT! MI JÁRATBAN ERREFELÉ?
ELVONT SÖRÉNY, HATALMAS SÁMÁN! KÉRLEK SEGÍTS RAJTAM!
ERŐS FÉRJEM, ÁZOTT SÓDER HETEK ÓTA HOZZÁM SEM ÉR... KÉSZÍTS VÁGYKELTŐ FŐZET, MELYET ÉTELÉBE CSEMPÉSZHETEK CSEPPENKÉNT.

source.text: CSEPPENKÉNT? EGY VÖDÖRRE MONDD, HOGY „LEVES”, ÚGY ADD NEKI, MÁR NE IS HARAGUDJ, PATENT!
lines: „LEVES”, ÚGY ADD NEKI, MÁR NE IS

lines: PA... PATENT... EH... MI LENNE, HA

source.text: IPARKODJ, ÉS ÉN JAVAS EMBERT CSINÁLOK BELŐLED. LEGYEN ENNYI ELÉG. VÉN HURON!

scene.summary: A Native American woman named Szakadt Patent (Torn Popper) visits the local shaman, Elvont Sörény (Abstract Mane), seeking an aphrodisiac potion because her husband hasn't touched her in weeks. The shaman insults her, suggesting she'd need an entire bucket of potion disguised as soup for her husband to desire her. However, when she flashes him her hidden physique beneath her robe, the shaman is instantly smitten and desperately begs her to run away with him to start a new life in America. Unfazed, she rebuffs him and strictly commands the old medicine man to get back to brewing.

characters.name: shaman (Elvont Sörény)
characters.description: A Native American medicine man with a single feather in his hair, working behind an apothecary table with herbs, potions, and a boiling pot. Initially sarcastic and crude, he becomes instantly aroused, stammering, and desperate upon seeing Szakadt Patent naked.

characters.name: Native American woman (Szakadt Patent)
characters.description: A Native American woman with braided hair wearing a simple robe. Pragmatic, assertive, and unimpressed by the shaman's sarcasm or advances.

panels.description: In a shaman's teepee/hut, Elvont Sörény sits behind a table with herbs and bottles, greeting Szakadt Patent, who stands before him asking for help.

Szakadt Patent explains that her husband no longer touches her and asks for an aphrodisiac to slip into his food drop by drop; the shaman laughs nastily, telling her she should feed him an entire bucket of it disguised as soup.
Szakadt Patent opens her robe to reveal her body to the shaman; the shaman's eyes pop wide open in stunned shock, and even the dog/pelt lying by the table reacts in surprise.
A drooling, hyperventilating shaman stammers and proposes that the two of them start a new life together in America, while Szakadt Patent walks off dismissively, telling the old Huron to get to work.

notes: The comic parodies Western/Karl May-style Native American naming conventions by combining poetic-sounding Indian names with completely mundane, absurd Hungarian words: 'Elvont Sörény' (Abstract Mane), 'Szakadt Patent' (Torn Snap-fastener / Ragged Press-stud), and 'Ázott Sóder' (Soaked Gravel / Soaked Bullshit).

In r3, the shaman delivers a brutal insult about her perceived unattractiveness: 'Cseppenként? Egy vödörre mondd, hogy „leves”, úgy add neki' ('Drop by drop? Call a bucket of it "soup" and serve him that, no offence, Patent!').

The anachronistic/meta-joke in r5: the shaman, overwhelmed by lust, suggests they start a new life together in America ('új élet kezdenénk Amerikában???'), ignoring the fact that they are already indigenous people in pre-modern America. The grammar in r5 is also casually clipped ('új élet [hiányzó tárgyrag: életet] kezdenénk').

In r6, 'javas ember' is traditional Hungarian folklore terminology for an herbalist / wise folk-healer / medicine man. Calling him 'vén huron' (old Huron) is a nod to Cooper/Karl May-era frontier adventure novels.

r0.text: SEI GEGRÜSST, KAPUTTER DRUCKKNOPF! WAS FÜHRT DICH HER?
r0.literal: Sei gegrüßt, Zerrissener Druckknopf! Was führt dich hierher?
r0.notes: Parody Native American name translated consistently.

r1.text: ABSTRAKTE MÄHNE, MÄCHTIGER SCHAMANE! BITTE HILF MIR!
r1.literal: Abstrakte Mähne, mächtiger Schamane! Bitte hilf mir!

r2.text: MEIN STARKER MANN NASSES GERÖLL RÜHRT MICH SEIT WOCHEN NICHT AN... BRAU EINEN LIEBESTRANK, DEN ICH IHM INS ESSEN TRÖPFLE.
r2.literal: Mein starker Mann, Durchnässter Kies, rührt mich seit Wochen nicht an... Braue ein Liebeselixier, das ich ihm tröpfchenweise ins Essen schmuggeln kann.

r3.text: TRÖPFELN? NENN EINEN GANZEN EIMER „SUPPE“ UND GIB IHM DEN, NICHT FÜR UNGUT, DRUCKKNOPF!
r3.literal: Tröpfchenweise? Sag zu einem Eimer voll „Suppe“ und gib ihm das so, nimm’s mir nicht übel, Druckknopf!

r4.notes: Shortened drastically to respect strict 29-character limit.

r5.text: DRUCK... DRUCKKNOPF... ÄH... WENN WIR BEIDE... IN AMERIKA NEU ANFANGEN???
r5.literal: Pa... Druckknopf... äh... was wäre, wenn wir beide... ein neues Leben beginnen in Amerika???
r5.notes: Kept the meta-joke about emigrating to America.

r6.text: MACH HIN, DANN MACH ICH EINEN MEDIZINMANN AUS DIR. DAS MUSS REICHEN, ALTER HURONE!
r6.literal: Beeil dich, und ich mache einen Heilkundigen aus dir. Das soll genügen, alter Hurone!
r6.notes: Restored her dismissive line 'Das muss reichen'.
